newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MURDER SUSPECT MISSED AS POLICE WAIT FOR BRITISH WARRANT

British police have released a statement denying they're to blame for a bungle which meant Australian Federal Police could not arrest a couple wanted for questioning over a murder in the United Kingdom.
The body of murder suspect Clifford Harris was found floating in the Swan River in Perth yesterday.
Mr Harris was wanted for questioning over the murder of art teacher Janice Crompton, whose body was found in his truck in north Devon on Saturday.
Federal Police say they located Mr Harris and his wife Margaret at a Perth hotel, but had no power to arrest them without a warrant from British authorities.
Police in Devon have issued a statement saying they could not take any action until they received the authority of the British Crown Prosecution Service.
Australian Federal Police say Mr Harris' death is not being treated as suspicious.
QLD PREMIER RESISTS FEDERALLY OPPOSED BUDGET CUTS
Queensland Premier, Rob Borbidge, says he's hopeful the Federal Government won't expect the states to help reel-in the latest budget deficit blowout.
Mr Borbidge says states and territories will have no choice but to raise taxes or reduce services if the Federal Government makes cuts to state funding.
He says Treasurer, Peter Costello, should honour an agreement struck at last year's Premiers' conference which set out an agreed agenda for spending cutbacks to the states.
Mr Borbidge says the willingness last year of states and territories to agree to budget cuts should be taken into account.
TELSTRA, OPTUS IN WAR OF WORDS OVER LOCAL CALLS
Telecommunications rivals, Telstra and Optus, have clashed over the issue of phone number portability once the system's deregulated.
Telstra says phone users wanting to switch carriers but retain their existing numbers could pay more than 30 cents for a local call, as opposed to the current 25 cents.
Optus says this is a barrier to competition, and has asked industry regulator, AUSTEL, to rule on the matter.
The dispute emerged during a Senate inquiry into the Government's intention to allow an unlimited number of phone companies into the local call market from July.
The inquiry is seen by new players as a way of bringing tougher regulatory controls into play, but Telstra says the new companies may exploit rules on untimed local calls.
SYDNEY'S LORD MAYOR GOES TO LONDON
One of the oldest local government authorities in the world is playing host to Sydney Lord Mayor, Frank Sartor.
Councillor Sartor has been holding talks with the Lord Mayor of London, Roger Cork, and members of the 800-year-old Corporation of London.

During his visit to Europe, Mr Sartor is also talking to potential suppliers for a range of public works projects to improve the appearance of central Sydney, and public security, in the run-up to the Olympics.
STATES CALLED TO UNITE ON TOURISM PUSH
The new head of the Australian Tourist Commission, John Morse, says the states and territories must cooperate in the overseas marketing push in the lead-up to the Sydney Olympics.
Mr Morse says domestic competition is healthy, but the states and territories must learn to work together.
He says state and federal money should be spent to promote Australia as a whole, rather than playing one region off against another.
Mr Morse says one of his aims over the next four years as Managing Director of the commission is to present a more united front for the industry.
QUEENSLAND POLICE START CHILD SEX CRIMES TASKFORCE
The Queensland police service is doubling the size of its Child Exploitation Unit to deal with an increase of paedophilia allegations over recent months.
Police Minister Russell Cooper says the unit will become a dedicated taskforce into paedophile activity.
The unit will go from nine to 20 officers.
STANDOFF MAN FOUND DEAD IN HOUSE
An armed man who kept police at bay for more than 25 hours, has been found dead on his Wee Jasper property, near Yass, north of Canberra.
The 50-year-old man was found dead in his bathroom last night, believed to have died from a self inflicted gunshot wound to the head.
The man had been barricaded inside his home since Tuesday afternoon, and was believed to be angry about a court case which resulted in him being given an apprehended violence order.
Police negotiators had arranged for the man to surrender yesterday morning, but the deadline passed when the man became angry at media coverage of the standoff.
Police raided the property after losing contact with the man for several hours.
MAKING NEWS IN SPORT
In GOLF...The $1.2 million Heineken Golf Classic begins this morning at the Vines, in Perth's Swan Valley.
It's arguably the best field ever assembled in Perth, headed by Ernie Els, Ian Woosnam, Fred Couples and Colin Montgomerie.
The tournament is part of the European tour, with many players needing to perform well to gain a place in the Ryder Cup team later this year.
CRICKET
GABBA curator Kevin Mitchell junior predicts a lively track for the day-night shield match between Queensland and Western Australia beginning tonight.
Rain has hampered pitch preparation all week with showers and high humidity expected for Brisbane for the duration of the match.
A dicey track meant last year's corresponding day-night match against New South Wales was over inside three days.
Mitchell says he expects this pitch to be worse.
Western Australian batsman Simon Katich may make his first class debut in place of spinner Brett Mulder.
And in the one-day match in Cape Town, Zimbabwe has made 226 against South Africa.
SWIMMING
Australia's Michael Klim has swum to his fourth victory in the World Cup meeting in Glasgow.
Klim won the 100 metres butterfly in 52-point-09 seconds, just two-hundredths of a second outside the world mark.
Just before that, he was victorious in the 200 metres freestyle, which followed wins a day earlier in the 100 metres freestyle and the 50 metres butterfly.
